format: Shared by the TypeScript tests (api/__tests__/futures-contracts.test.ts) and by the Python tests of the uw-stream futures_trades handler (uw-stream/tests/test_futures_front_month.py), which run the `cmeTradeDate` and `decideFrontMonth` lists against their port of the per-session front-month rule. The `pickScheduledFront` list is TypeScript-only: it is the REST minute builder, which picks the larger-volume spelling's row, where the live handler folds both spellings' prints into one bar. Three lists, each case with a unique `name`. `cmeTradeDate`: {name, ts, tradeDate}. ts is a UTC instant (ISO, ending in Z). Its CME trade date is the America/Chicago calendar date of ts + 7 hours, so a session runs from 17:00 Chicago time on the evening before its trade date until 17:00 on it (the open moves between 22:00Z and 23:00Z with daylight saving). `decideFrontMonth`: {name, root, tradeDate, incumbent, volumes, front}. Run decide(incumbent, volumes, root, tradeDate) and compare it with `front`. incumbent is a contract symbol or null (none). volumes is an object of contract symbol to volume, symbols as fed. Every symbol, the incumbent included, is first folded to its canonical name: root, CME month code and the last year digit, so ESZ26 is ESZ6 and the spellings of one contract sum their volumes. A symbol that is not an outright of `root` (a spread, another root) is dropped, and so is a two-digit year outside the one-digit window [Y - 1, Y + 8], Y being the year of tradeDate. A one-digit year is the one year in that window ending in that digit. `front` is always a canonical name. With no incumbent and no volume left, the result is the first contract in the root's listing cycle that has not stopped trading by the month of tradeDate. `pickScheduledFront`: {name, schedule, rows, picked}. schedule maps a trade date to a contract name, and a trade date it does not list has no scheduled contract. rows is a list of {key, ts, volume}: build one list of rows per key, keys in order of first appearance, and run pick(byKey, contractFor), where contractFor looks a trade date up in schedule. A row counts only if the canonical name of its key, with Y taken from the trade date of the row's own ts, equals the scheduled contract of that trade date (canonical too). Of several counting rows in one minute (two spellings of one contract) the larger volume's row is picked, and a tie goes to the key that sorts first by code point, whatever the order of the rows. A minute where the scheduled contract has no counting row is left out. Compare the result with `picked` exactly, in time order: {ts, contract, key, volume}, where contract is the scheduled canonical name, key is the key (spelling) whose own row it is and volume is that row's own volume, not a sum. A case may have `throws` instead of `front` (decideFrontMonth) or `picked` (pickScheduledFront). Then the call must raise an error and return nothing, and the TypeScript tests also match the error message against `throws`, a regular expression tried anywhere in it. A port must raise, and its message should name the same things, but may be checked on the raise alone. For decideFrontMonth the error is a stored incumbent that, once folded, is not an outright of `root` (another root, a spread, a bare root, a two-digit year outside the window, an empty string). That is a corrupt row, and reading it as no incumbent would reseed over it and pass every other case. For pickScheduledFront the error is a scheduled name that, once folded, is not an outright of any root. It is raised when a row falls on that trade date, so a bad schedule is not read as a quiet day.
